Idea: Have a cheap and easy way to make logging water fountains easier. NFC tags will be placed on or near the water fountains, where they can be scanned by phones to instantly log a fountain, reducing the effort of logging and incentivizing app use. A secondary use is to grab the user’s location on scan, which will be entered into the app (with permission) along with the tag’s ID, strengthening the precision of the location of the fountain with each scan.

NFC tags were supplied in two forms, a card and fob form (see fig 1.). Either will be suitable for demonstrating the NFC functionality. They’ll be programmed by a MIFARE RFID-RC522 module using an Arduino UNO and the Arduino IDE.

![][image1]  
Fig 1\. NFC tags in two forms

These tags are programmed at the 13.56MHz radio frequency, which NFC enabled phones (iPhone 7+ running ios 13+ and NFC enabled android devices) can read (GODBLESS). I won’t be adding encryption yetbecause idk how to do that but if this idea gets off the ground then it is definitely a good idea along with write lock. 

[https\://www\.instructables.com/Interfacing-RC522-RFID-Module-With-Arduino/](https://www.instructables.com/Interfacing-RC522-RFID-Module-With-Arduino/)   
I’ll be using this link to program my tags. Unfortunately, the tags supplied with this module AREN’T super supported by modern phones. They work under the common ISO14443A protocol, but aren’t a standard type (1-5) that phones expect. For the demo, i could probably use the RC522 to read  but ideally if I can find a type 2 (ISO14443A supporting) tag, then my RC522 can program it and a phone will read it.

OKOK im back yeah im ditching the RC522 tags. Phones are thankfully super cool now, and can program compatible NTAG215 tags. (see next page)
